messages.author: 9b48f0bcd1ff214c
messages.subject: What dose cov.bases do?
parts:
Hello
I am a bit confused about the 'cov.bases' option in tileMethylCounts.
Does it 1) filter entire windows using a criterion of minimum number of sites/bases with sufficient cover? e.g. the code below would remove windows that do not have at least 10 bases with sufficient cover (what is the cover value?).
or 2) filter windows that don't have a minimum cover (average across the window, maybe), so in the example below, windows without a minimum coverage of 10 reads (average?) will be removed.
Or am I completely misunderstanding what it does.
 
'''
tiles = tileMethylCounts(myobj_lowCov,win.size=1000,step.size=1000,cov.bases = 10)
'''

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: What dose cov.bases do?
parts:
Hi Ryan, 

as you can see in the code the `cov.bases` is basically forwarded to the regionCounts function after defining the tiles. The counts for all bases within tiles will be summed up and any tile not reaching a coverage of at least `cov.bases` will be discarded (see code). 

I hope this explains what `cov.bases´ stands for. 

Best,
Alex

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: What dose cov.bases do?
parts:
Hi Ryan, 

Sorry, but the previous answer that I gave you was wrong. Your first assumption was correct.

Given your example, this would first create non-overlapping tiles of length 1000 (since win.size == step.size) that will cover all sites in your ´myobj_lowCov`. Then for each tile, the number of underlying sites/bases would be determined and tiles that do not include at least 10 sites/bases are discarded.  
The cover value here is independent of the specific site's coverage, each base adds a single count towards the covered bases. 

Best,
Alex
